intro: Social media managers charge by choosing between hourly rates, flat monthly retainers, or value-based project fees. Determining the right model depends on your specific service scope, the complexity of the client accounts, and your target profit margins.

blocks.text: Why social media pricing strategy is difficult

Pricing is often the hardest part of running a social media business. You lack industry standards. Platforms change every month. It is difficult to separate the value of your strategic advice from the time spent on manual tasks. Many managers fall into the trap of setting prices based on what feels comfortable rather than what the business requires to stay profitable.

Undercharging is the fastest way to burnout. When you do not account for every hour, you end up working for pennies. This limits your ability to scale. You cannot hire help or buy better tools if your margins are too thin. You may also attract the wrong clients. Clients who want the cheapest price are often the ones who demand the most extra work.
How to fix your pricing without new software

items: Create three standard packages: Basic, Standard, and Premium.
Define exactly how many posts, stories, and reports are included.
Set a strict policy for extra revisions or platforms.
Always bill ad spend as a separate line item.
Track your time in a simple spreadsheet to see your real hourly rate.

faq.question: Should I charge hourly or by the project?
faq.answer: Most professional managers prefer monthly retainers. They provide predictable income and allow you to focus on results rather than counting every minute.

faq.question: How do I deal with scope creep?
faq.answer: Put everything in writing. If a client asks for extra work, refer them to your contract and offer a separate quote for the additional service.

costs.title: Burnout
costs.text: Working long hours for low pay leads to exhaustion and loss of passion for your work.

costs.title: Stunted Growth
costs.text: Low margins prevent you from hiring help or investing in better tools for your agency.

causes.title: Lack of Standards
causes.text: The industry is young and lacks a single pricing model, making it hard to know where to start.

causes.title: Scope Creep
causes.text: Failing to define what is included leads to doing extra work for free.

fixes.title: Standardized Packages
fixes.text: Define clear service tiers so clients know exactly what they are paying for.

fixes.title: Separate Ad Spend
fixes.text: Never include ad budgets in your management fee to maintain clear profit margins.
